Vartika 'ṛti savarṇe ṛ vā': optional two-more (dvimātra) ṛ with a double r in the middle (Kaumudi), otherwise ordinary dirgha ṝ. Laghu lists hotṝkāraḥ only.
Vartika 'ḷti savarṇe ḷ vā': a special double-l vowel or, in the other option, ṝ by savarnya (ḷ has no long).

Neuter dual: au -> śī (7.1.19); a + ī -> e. Without 6.1.104 the purvasavarnadirgha would give kuṇḍā.
Kaumudi: after 6.1.104 blocks 6.1.102, guna ādguṇaḥ and then eṅaḥ padāntād ati give śivo'rcyaḥ. Balamanorama on 6.1.102 starts from the stage 'śiva u arcya' (the particle u). Flag nipata on u.

ā + a of jas: the prohibition holds, and 6.1.101 (savarnadirgha) gives the same ā. Kaumudi: even if purvasavarnadirgha applied the result would be viśvapāḥ, so the sutra is placed here for gauryau etc.
Kaumudi: 'gauryau gaurya' are the reason for the sutra (long ī before an ic).
Vedic: after a long vowel before jas the prohibition of 6.1.105 is optional, so either ī (purvasavarnadirgha) or yaṇ. Kasika: mārutīś catasraḥ piṇḍīḥ / mārutyaś catasraḥ piṇḍyaḥ. Flag stem:jas.
Vedic dual: purvasavarnadirgha (vārāhī) or yaṇ (vārāhyau); both listed by Kaumudi/Kasika.
Vedic: Kaumudi says 6.1.106's option is carried forward to 6.1.107 and 6.1.108 'vakyabhedena': so purvarupa (śamīm) or yaṇ (śamyam) before am.

Balamanorama: 6.1.101 (dirgha) is displaced by 6.1.97 (pararupa), which is displaced by 6.1.102 (purvasavarnadirgha), which is displaced by 6.1.107.

yaj + kta (nom. sg. neuter am): samprasarana y -> i (6.1.15), then i + a -> i (purvarupa, 6.1.108) instead of yaṇ; then ṣ and ṭ by 8.3.59/8.4.41. The source states only the form; the intermediate steps are the standard ones. Input is my reading.

ṅasi/ṅas after guna e: e + a of as -> e (purvarupa), then s -> ru -> r before a vowel (agner āgacchati) and visarga in pause/before s (agneḥ svam). Apadanta case (the e is not pada-final), which is why 6.1.109 cannot cover it.

Kasika: ṛ + a of ṅas/ṅasi -> u, with raparatva by 1.1.51 (the sthanin is shared: 'dvayoh sasthinirdistayoh sthane yah sa labhate 'nyataravyapadesam'), then 8.2.24 (rat sasya) drops the s after the r: hotur āgacchati / hotuḥ svam. The rule itself is not restricted to hotṛ: also pitṛ, kartṛ, dātṛ. Flag stem:ṅas.
sakhi + ṅas: after the yaṇ (sakhy), the a of ṅas becomes u (not the pair): sakhyuḥ. The input sakhy is the stem with the yaṇ already made ('krtayanadesa'). Flag stem:ṅas.

ānaṅ replaces the ṛ (the LAST sound) of mātṛ only, because the substitute is ṅit (ṅicca 1.1.53), not the whole stem (which 1.1.55 anekāl would give). Kasika also lists hotāpotārau. The third word is the dual au; split by me.

īdāsaḥ (7.2.83): ī is substituted for the FIRST sound of the following ā-na (ādeḥ parasya), because the rule is worded with the ablative. Kasika gives āsīno yajate. Also dvīpam, antarīpam, pratīpam, samīpam (6.3.97).

source.quote: इति स्थानिवत्त्वात् सुपि चेति दीर्घः। रामाय

notes: The substitute ya for ṅe counts as a Sup (sthanivat, 1.1.56), so 7.3.102 (supi ca) lengthens the a. The rule 1.1.56 is limited to non-al-vidhi (analvidhau). The sutras field puts 7.1.13 (ṅeryaḥ) first as the adesa.

1.1.58 (na padantadvirvacana...) forbids sthanivadbhava for dvitva: the yaṇ y is not treated as a vowel, so the optional doubling of dh (8.4.47 anaci ca) can happen. If y were a vowel (sthanivat) dh would not double. Both forms are accepted (doubling is optional).

1.1.59 (dvirvacane 'ci): the yaṇ substituted before the vowel-initial atus (tus of perfect dual) is treated as the vowel r for the purpose of the dvitva (reduplication), otherwise anackatvāt the reduplication would not happen. Split by me; reduplication vowel/consonant changes not shown.
